edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource; the variant readings it marks are left out. Lines broken at the punctuation for reading; text unchanged.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，删去其所注异文。按标点分行，文字未改。

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died in 754.

note.en: A story told in later collections says Li Bai climbed this tower, read Cui Hao’s poem on the wall, and put down his brush, saying the view had already been written. Whether or not it happened, the poem earns it: the yellow crane three times in the first three lines, the rules of regulated verse broken on purpose, and then a sudden clear view of trees and grass across the river. The crane is the past; the tower is what is left of it.
note.zh: 后世笔记里有个故事：李白登上黄鹤楼，读到崔颢题在壁上的诗，便搁笔说“眼前有景道不得，崔颢题诗在上头”。不论真假，这首诗担得起：前三句三次出现“黄鹤”，有意打破律诗的规矩，然后忽然一片清朗，望见对岸的树和草。黄鹤是过去，楼是过去留下的东西。

excerpt.orig: 黃鶴一去不復返，白雲千載空悠悠。
excerpt.en: The yellow crane, once gone, never came back; / for a thousand years the white clouds have drifted, empty.
excerpt.zh: 黄鹤一去不复返，白云千载空悠悠。

gloss.en: In legend an immortal, named in different sources as Fei Yi or Zi’an, rode off from here on a yellow crane. The tower stood above the Yangzi at Wuchang, in present-day Wuhan.
gloss.zh: 传说仙人（一说费祎，一说子安）曾在此乘黄鹤而去。黄鹤楼故址在今湖北武汉武昌，下临长江。

gloss.en: Clear and distinct, one by one.
Hanyang, across the river from the tower.
gloss.zh: 汉阳：地名，在今武汉，与黄鹤楼隔江相望。

gloss.en: Parrot Island, a sandbar in the Yangzi; the Tang island was later washed away.
gloss.zh: 鹦鹉洲：长江中的沙洲，唐时的鹦鹉洲后被江水冲没。
